Sourcing the PKGBUILD only evaluates variable declarations, which are safe and non-malicious. The provided `snapper-rollback.install` script contains only standard post-install and post-upgrade hooks used during package installation or update in Arch Linux. The `post_install` function checks for the presence of a `.pacsave` configuration file (created by pacman when replacing a config file) and, if found, extracts values from it using `awk` to migrate settings to the new configuration file `/etc/snapper-rollback.conf`. The migration uses safe parsing techniques (field splitting on `=`) and only modifies the new config if the old one exists.

The operations performed—reading from a local config file, extracting values with `awk`, updating another config with `sed`, and printing a message to stderr—are all expected behaviors for a configuration migration during a package upgrade. No network activity, code execution, or file operations outside the configuration scope are present. The script does not exfiltrate data, execute remote code, or perform any suspicious system modifications.

This script aligns with standard AUR and Arch Linux packaging practices for handling configuration file transitions. There are no signs of obfuscation, malicious payloads, or supply-chain attacks.
</details>

There are no network operations, file manipulations, or system modifications performed by this file itself. The package depends only on standard system utilities (coreutils, python, btrfs-progs), which are expected for a script managing btrfs snapshots via snapper.
